UK LOCATION GUIDES

Parrots for Birmingham homes

Birmingham is in the West Midlands, with households and living arrangements that differ from one another. Before considering a bird, bring everyone affected into the conversation and test whether the daily responsibilities and environment work for the household as a whole.

Regional planning guide

This page helps owners prepare an enquiry. It is not evidence of local Crownwing premises, local stock or a confirmed collection or delivery service.

Make the choice a household decision

List the concerns each person has about sound, cleaning, time and interaction. A parrot changes the shared home even when one adult takes primary responsibility, so agreement should cover ordinary care as well as the excitement of bringing a bird home.

Consider children, visitors and other animals without assuming that a bird will welcome contact. Establish adult supervision, secure boundaries and quiet opportunities for the bird to move away from attention.

Look beyond a group label

African Grey Parrots, Amazons and small psittacines each cover a range of birds and needs. Compare the exact species for vocal behaviour, social interaction, enrichment and likely adult size instead of using a broad category as a personality prediction.

Ask what is known about the particular bird’s responses to handling, new surroundings and different people. A description such as confident or friendly needs context and does not guarantee how the bird will behave with every member of a household.

Agree who does what each day

Name the person responsible for routine tasks and decide how everyone else can help. Set up a simple way to share information about food, cleaning and observed preferences so changes in household availability do not leave basic care uncertain.

Make sure the main carer has time for species-appropriate exercise and interaction. If care is shared, each person should understand the bird’s boundaries and avoid forcing handling to create a quick bond.

Prepare a safe, usable area

Review where an enclosure can stand without blocking household movement and how the bird could have supervised time outside it. Check doors, windows, cooking areas and access by other pets as part of the room plan.

Equipment should fit the exact bird’s size and beak strength. Ask what the individual currently uses and what familiar items, food or routines may help make a move less confusing.

Questions to bring to an enquiry

Ask for the exact species, known age, current diet, background and available records. Clarify what is known about social experience, vocal habits and handling preferences, and request recent information about the actual bird rather than relying on a generic species image.

Explain who lives in the home, what experience is present and how care would be shared. Ask what further preparation is recommended and what terms or arrangements would need separate confirmation.

Confirm arrangements before making travel plans

No local viewing, collection point or transport arrangement is established by reading this guide. If an enquiry concerns a specific bird, ask directly whether a handover option can be agreed and who would be responsible for its details.

Only plan travel after the location, timing and appropriate carrier have been discussed and confirmed. Keep a written record of what has been agreed and make sure the bird’s routine and welfare remain central.
